extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians, stand-up performers, and comedy writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for constructing three-part jokes (setup, turn/punch, tag) and evaluating joke drafts for clarity, surprise, and extendability; includes authentic topic sourcing and a five-section workbook system for developing material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundational element introducing the premise; sets the stage for the audience and establishes the scenario or 'the normal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates anticipation and guides listeners toward the punchline. Should be clear, concise, and grounded in relatability. Establish the 'normal' so the turn can pivot meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turn (Punch)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unexpected twist — the pivot in meaning where the laugh happens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be a clean, surprising pivot from the setup. The effectiveness depends on how well the setup guides the audience into an expectation that the turn subverts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional punch line that doesn't need a new setup; extends the original premise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to maximize laughs from a single setup by adding successive punches. Tags should build on the established premise rather than introducing new setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic Topic Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use personal experiences (childhood, relationships, jobs, special challenges) as material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics drawn from authentic experience resonate more because they're relatable. Choose specifics from your life to increase originality and audience connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 5-Section Workbook System
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured system for developing material: 1) 48 Exercises to Turn Problems into Punchlines; 2) Jokes in Progress by Topic; 3) My Act: Polished Jokes by Topic; 4) Set Lists for organizing material by time and theme; 5) Morning Writings — 30 prompts to create material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exercises to generate raw premises and turns, track jokes-in-progress by topic, transfer polished jokes into 'My Act', organize performance-ready material with set lists, and maintain daily writing habit with morning prompts to continuously produce new fodder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the setup clear, concise, relatable?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation question: Is the setup clear, concise, relatable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks whether the audience can quickly grasp the 'normal' and form an expectation. Relatability anchors the setup and brevity prevents dilution of the eventual turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a clean turn (twist)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation question: Is there a clean turn (twist)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the punch pivot is distinct and surprising relative to the setup. A clean turn avoids muddled or ambiguous pivots that fail to produce a laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are tags possible to extend?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation question: Are tags possible to extend?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines if the premise supports additional punch lines without new setups. Good premises often yield multiple tags to increase laugh density.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the topic come from authentic experience?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation question: Does the topic come from authentic experience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures originality and relatability: material rooted in real life tends to connect better with audiences than borrowed or generic topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the audience guided into a clear expectation before the turn?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation question: Is the audience guided into a clear expectation before the turn?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the setup effectively funnels listeners toward a predictable interpretation that the turn can subvert. Without a clear expectation the twist will have less impact.
